newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower as bears reign.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower as bears reign.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Monday due to the dollar's weakness against the yen and worries about Japan's construction and financial sectors.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 170 points lower at 19,760 on volume of 16,515 lots.
Dealers said a medium-sized construction firm's decision to apply for court protection from its creditors on Friday had triggered fears of more bad debts at Japanese banks.
"People are worried that there may be other construction companies having similar problems and banks' bad debts could be worse than announced," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
He said the dollar's fall below 113 yen after the release of Japan's June first 20-days trade data, showing a higher surplus than the same period a year ago, dragged the market down in early trade.
The dollar was quoted at 112.25/35 yen at 0752 GMT.
"The dollar/yen doesn't look too good now. If it goes lower tomorrow, the Nikkei could fall below support at 19,700 and test 19,550 tomorrow," he said.
Dealers said the September Nikkei's upside was likely to be capped around 20,000 for the time being.
The July MSCI Taiwan index contract ended higher at 399.0 on volume of 942 lots.
